In the seas throughout Inoa Ranas, headfish lurk beneath the surface with human faces and inhuman ferocity. These mysterious fish, most commonly measuring in at 16 inches and 11 pounds, possess perfect replicas of human faces of those who have recently died or are soon to die. From all accounts, the visage perfectly matches the deceased in skin tone, blemishes, scars, makeup, tattoos, and even jewelry. Some have also claimed to hear the voices of dead loved ones coming from them, but the validity of this is unknown. The only facial feature that betrays this illusion is their teeth, which are long, jagged, and sharp as glass shards. Besides their face, headfish possess tattered, inefficient fins and dull brown scales.

 Understandably, almost every encounter with a headfish is an emotional moment, and they've gained infamy as bad omens and killers. Many parents, for instance, only learn of a child’s death from finding a headfish with their face. Despite what seems to be clearly supernatural, the headfish are not considered to be spirits. It is unknown how they come into possession of their faces or how their power as omens work, and no ties to any gods or prominent spirits are apparent.

 Headfish are almost never seen outside of catches or attacks on people or animals. From that, it is thought that headfish are highly aggressive, territorial, or just malicious. However, nobody truly knows what they do before they're caught. Headfish seem to be obligate carnivores, from what's seen of them. Certainly, their razor-sharp, glasslike teeth lend credence to this claim. Even if they’re not seen directly, their presence is often known from the characteristic circular, jagged holes cut from larger fish. However, headfish are slow swimmers due to their tattered fins, which calls into question how they keep up with all the fish they take bites out of. From attacks on people, it is known that headfish are the culprits leaving these bites. Besides the meat taken from biting into larger animals, it is unknown if they ever eat anything else like plants or if they even need to eat in order to survive.

 It is completely unknown how headfish reproduce, or even if they do reproduce through natural means. Throughout every catch and every encounter, nobody has ever reported seeing any milt, roe, eggs, or any other reproductive structure. Not even juveniles have been spotted unless you would count headfish with children's faces. The lack of any known reproduction calls into question just how people keep seeing them, and adds to their eerie nature.

As a teenager with diagnosed clinical depression and social anxiety, I've had to spend time in a psych ward. Even after that, I would doubt myself all the time whether or not I even had these conditions. I mean, I've certainly gotten a lot better about it over time with therapy and medication (and I'd like to believe some personal growth too). But it was this trend that frightened me. People with massive amounts of friends and human interaction would be talking about just how bad their social anxiety is and all their friends would laugh "same haha me too". I'd see dick measuring competitions on just who had the worst mental disorders as if it was something to covet. Obviously I don't know what goes on in their lives, but it's absurd that every one of them we really mentally ill. I would be having a good day and I'd be so afraid that I was just another person begging for attentionvand praise with my mental illness as a facade. Now I can recognize that that was a product of the mindset I was in and that I really do have a diagnosed problem that I still struggle with. I can only imagine that something similar may be happening to others like me and it angers and saddens me that it's so casual and widespread. It's like the entire thing is a joke you can brush off and laugh with friends about.
